article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Early Skunk × Sensi Star
Breeder: Magus Genetics / Gerrit Slot
THC Content: 26%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet mint, blonde hash, earthy Skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 50–60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: September / October
Indoor Yield: Good
Outdoor Yield: Good
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Biddy’s Sister was created to solve a very practical problem. Magus Genetics already had Biddy Early , an acclaimed outdoor cultivar capable of producing excellent marijuana in the relatively unforgiving Dutch climate, but breeder Gerrit Slot wanted something shorter, earlier, and more convenient indoors without abandoning the rugged outdoor qualities of the family. His answer was to retain Early Skunk as one side of the pedigree and replace Biddy Early’s Warlock influence with Sensi Star, a compact, resin-heavy indica classic. The result earned the affectionate “little sister” name because its flowering stretch was restrained and its indoor structure better suited to tight Sea of Green gardens . Given enough vegetative time outdoors, however, the little sister could become anything but small. Gerrit reported plants reaching around 2.5 meters with enormous lateral development.

That combination of manageable indoor architecture and serious outdoor vigor eventually earned recognition beyond Magus Genetics’ catalog. At the 2008 Highlife Cup in Holland, Biddy’s Sister placed first in the Seed Company Outdoor Weed category, finishing ahead of Reserva Privada ’s Coletrain and Catweazle Seeds’ Moonflower. Its reputation rested on more than garden performance. The strain developed a strong but pleasantly sweet aroma early in life, while cured flower moved toward mint, resin, and the distinctive character of high-quality blonde Moroccan hash . The high followed the Sensi Star direction without becoming overwhelmingly narcotic: relaxing in the body, substantial in potency, yet comparatively comfortable and functional.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct cross is Early Skunk × Sensi Star. Gerrit Slot confirmed that pedigree himself in correspondence with growers and explained the reasoning behind it. Biddy Early already paired Early Skunk with Warlock. For Biddy’s Sister, Magus substituted Sensi Star specifically to produce a shorter, more indica-oriented plant expected to finish about one week sooner than its famous half-sibling. That makes the relationship between the two cannabis strains unusually straightforward: they share the Early Skunk side but use different fathers to pursue different horticultural goals.

Early Skunk brings formidable outdoor genetics to the cross. Sensi Seeds developed that parent from Skunk #1 × Early Pearl, combining the large yields and pungent hybrid character of Skunk with the earlier maturation and outdoor resilience of Early Pearl. Sensi currently describes Early Skunk as a 65% indica / 35% sativa hybrid capable of producing very large plants and dense flowers while performing reliably in cooler, wetter climates. It was specifically bred to improve resistance to mold and bud rot—traits of obvious value to a Dutch breeder working on an early-finishing outdoor cultivar.

Sensi Star changes the character substantially. Paradise Seeds ’ famous indica-dominant cultivar contributed compact growth, heavy resin, dense flowers, and a much stronger body-oriented dimension. Rather than simply making a faster Biddy Early, the cross created a hybrid with its own personality. The Early Skunk side supplies vigor, branching, outdoor adaptability, and a touch of brighter hybrid effect, while Sensi Star pushes the finished plant toward lower stretch, resinous flowers, hash-like flavor, and deeper physical relaxation.
Effects and Experience

Biddy’s Sister was never marketed as a strain designed to overwhelm experienced smokers. Gerrit described the finished effect as a pleasant, body-relaxing stone that was potent without becoming devastatingly strong. That wording captures the cultivar better than assigning it an arbitrary modern indica percentage. The first phase can retain enough mental clarity to make conversation, music, reading, or a quiet afternoon enjoyable, but there is little of the racing cerebral intensity associated with long-flowering Haze strains .

As the experience settles, the physical side becomes more noticeable. Muscular tension can feel less important, movement becomes slower and more deliberate, and the session takes on the comfortable weight associated with classic indica-influenced marijuana. Sensi Star’s presence is particularly evident here, although Early Skunk prevents the effect from feeling completely flat. The progression is more gradual than abrupt: mental ease first, followed by a warmer physical calm that can make the cultivar especially appealing later in the day.

There is no reliable breeder-issued THC percentage for the original release, so modern numbers attached to the name should be treated cautiously. Biddy’s Sister disappeared from commercial preservation after Magus Genetics, making contemporary laboratory-tested flower especially difficult to authenticate. Potency should therefore be judged from the actual product rather than a historical percentage copied across strain databases. As with other THC-rich weed, excessive consumption may cause dizziness, dry mouth, impaired coordination, anxiety, memory disruption, or unwanted sedation.
Medical Benefits

No controlled clinical research has investigated Biddy’s Sister itself as a treatment for any medical condition. Its relaxing body effect historically made it attractive to consumers seeking a calmer style of cannabis, but anecdotal strain reputation should be separated from clinical evidence. A seed-grown cultivar also cannot be assumed to produce identical cannabinoid ratios from one plant or harvest to another.

Cannabis research more broadly provides limited context. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes that certain cannabis-derived preparations may reduce some forms of chronic pain in the short term, although dizziness and sleepiness can occur. Research involving cannabis and sleep has sometimes found improved sleep quality or fewer disturbances among patients with underlying health problems, but it remains uncertain whether cannabinoids directly improve sleep or whether symptom relief explains the change.

Those findings do not mean Biddy’s Sister specifically treats pain, insomnia, anxiety, or another disorder. THC can impair concentration and coordination and may aggravate anxiety in susceptible individuals. Cannabinoids can also interact with medications. Anyone using marijuana for persistent symptoms should rely on current product testing and appropriate medical guidance rather than the historical reputation of an older strain.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweetness appears remarkably early in the plant’s life. Magus Genetics noted that Biddy’s Sister developed a strong but pleasant sweet aroma well before flowering was complete, making odor control relevant even during earlier stages of cultivation. The finished flowers preserve some of that sweetness but shift toward a far more distinctive flavor once consumed. Rather than fruit candy or dessert cream, mint becomes the dominant impression.

Gerrit compared the flavor with quality blonde Moroccan hashish, an unusually specific description that helps separate this cultivar from conventional Skunk hybrids. The profile can be understood as sweet resin combined with cool mint, dry herbs, subtle earth, and spicy hash. Early Skunk contributes its earthy and pungent foundation, while Sensi Star supplies the denser resinous, metallic-herbal character that made that parent famous. The result feels distinctly European and old school rather than tropical or confectionery.

No credible laboratory terpene analysis from the original Magus line survives, so assigning specific dominant terpene percentages would be speculative. The historical sensory description is considerably more trustworthy: sweet aroma during growth, sweetness in the smoke, and a pronounced minty, blonde-hash character on the palate. Proper drying and curing would have been essential for preserving those lighter herbal and mint notes, since excessive heat tends to flatten volatile aromatics and leave primarily earth and resin behind.
Growing Information

Indoors, Biddy’s Sister was designed around efficiency. Gerrit chose Sensi Star because he wanted reduced stretch and a shorter plant than Biddy Early, making the resulting weed especially appropriate for Sea of Green cultivation. Historical specifications give approximately 50–60 days of flowering, while Gerrit personally estimated seven to eight weeks. The relatively compact flowering structure allows growers to run plants closer together without dealing with the dramatic vertical expansion associated with more sativa-dominant outdoor genetics.

Outdoors, the story changes completely. Limited flowering stretch does not mean the plant remains permanently compact. With a long vegetative period, Magus reported exceptional hybrid vigor. A plant started in early May could reach approximately 2.5 meters, with side branches rising nearly as high as the main stem and the central stalk becoming thick enough to resemble a small trunk. Harvest in Holland was estimated for the second half of September, giving the cultivar a meaningful advantage where wet autumn weather makes late-finishing marijuana risky.

Branch strength is the principal structural weakness. Although the central stalk can become massive, Magus warned that the lateral branches were relatively brittle and could split or tear at the nodes under strong winds, especially after heavy flowers developed. Outdoor plants therefore benefit from staking, cages, netting, or other structural support. This characteristic makes the plant easier to manage in a backyard or controlled garden than in unattended outdoor locations where repairs are difficult. Good airflow also remains important around mature flowers despite the Early Skunk parent’s reputation for outdoor resilience.

Yield was simply described by Magus Genetics as “good,” without a reliable numerical indoor or outdoor figure. That restraint should be preserved rather than replacing it with invented gram estimates. The plant’s architecture makes the context important: short SOG plants can produce efficiently indoors, while a long-season outdoor specimen can become enormous. Yield therefore depends heavily on vegetative duration, root volume, plant spacing, training, climate, and support.
FAQ
What strain is Biddy’s Sister?
Biddy’s Sister is an indica-leaning hybrid bred by Gerrit Slot of Magus Genetics from Early Skunk × Sensi Star. It was created as a shorter, earlier-flowering half-sibling to Biddy Early.
Is Biddy’s Sister related to Biddy Early?

Yes. Both share Early Skunk genetics. Biddy Early uses Warlock as the other parent, while Biddy’s Sister uses Sensi Star. Gerrit selected Sensi Star to make the newer hybrid shorter, more indica influenced, and approximately one week earlier finishing.
What does Biddy’s Sister taste like?

The original breeder described a sweet aroma with a predominantly minty flavor reminiscent of high-quality blonde Moroccan hashish. Earth, resin, Skunk, herbs, and gentle spice fill out the background.
How long does Biddy’s Sister take to flower?

Historical Magus Genetics information lists approximately 50–60 days indoors, with Gerrit estimating roughly seven to eight weeks. Outdoors in Holland, he expected plants to finish during the second half of September.
Did Biddy’s Sister win a cannabis award?
Yes. Magus Genetics’ Biddy’s Sister won 1st place in the Seed Company Outdoor Weed category at the 2008 Highlife Cup in Holland.
Final Thoughts on Biddy’s Sister

Biddy’s Sister is a particularly good example of purposeful cannabis breeding. Gerrit Slot was not trying to invent a flashy new name or simply combine two famous varieties. He already had Biddy Early and understood its strengths; what he wanted was a related plant that stayed shorter indoors and finished sooner outdoors. Crossing Early Skunk with Sensi Star accomplished that goal while creating a sufficiently distinctive strain to develop its own following.

Its 2008 Highlife Cup victory provides strong historical validation of the outdoor side of that breeding work. The cultivar took first place in the Seed Company Outdoor Weed category, demonstrating that a plant designed partly around practical northern-European cultivation could also produce competition-quality flower. The growth traits are unusually well documented: approximately 50–60 days indoors, limited flowering stretch, excellent hybrid vigor outdoors, potential heights around 2.5 meters with an early start, and lateral branches that benefit from support.

Flavor gives the strain an equally memorable identity. Instead of modern candy or creamy gas, Biddy’s Sister offers sweet mint, herbal resin, Skunk, and a blonde-Moroccan-hash character, followed by a comfortable body-oriented stone that Magus considered potent without being excessively overpowering.

There is also a bittersweet historical footnote. When Magus Genetics came under the Serious Seeds umbrella in 2012, Serious Seeds reported that the original mother plants for both Exile and Biddy’s Sister had already been lost, preventing the company from adding either strain to its continuing Magus catalog. That makes authentic surviving material especially significant. Biddy’s Sister is not merely another discontinued weed strain; it represents a documented piece of Dutch breeding history—Early Skunk × Sensi Star, created for earlier finishing and better indoor manageability, then proven outdoors with a first-place Highlife Cup result.
